analysis: Only CHANGELOG.md was supplied. Units 8 and 9 are base excerpts (lines 1381-1756) and unit 10 is the head excerpt (lines 1-232). No patch or source code was supplied, so no security behavior is verifiable beyond the changelog's claims. New head entries describe the following. (1) Autopilot daily earnings floor (head lines 5-7): new payments, admin funding and baseline-repair endpoints, and consent evidence; this is the basis of the one finding (A-009, TB-008, ADV-001). (2) Machine-scoped Autopilot desired mode in the database, with admin edit endpoints (lines 13-19); the coordinator-side live-control authority claims need checking against code (TB-002, TB-006). (3) Soft-delete mutation gate defaulting off, and account erasure (lines 81-105; T-059). (4) Removal of top-level user, metadata, safety_identifier and prompt_cache_key from provider-bound bodies, which also removes prompt_cache_key (line 230). T-041 already says cache scope is coordinator-derived and ignores caller keys. (5) SSD cache write-budget ledger (line 46). The changelog says the budget is persistent and root-wide; T-041 should mention endurance and DoS behavior if that is a mitigation. (6) PII removed from coordinator logs (line 113). (7) Bedrock/OpenRouter merge-review tooling (lines 30-38). The next pass should check the code behind the admin endpoints, the Autopilot baseline and alias handling, and the erasure mutation gate.

findings.detail: The changelog introduces a separately funded daily floor that pays providers a top-up when closed-UTC-day inference earnings fall below 110% of a seven-day baseline. The baseline is frozen at first opt-in and includes sponsored inference. It adds admin funding and baseline-repair endpoints, persistent consent evidence and per-machine receipts across identity aliases. This is a new money-moving surface on the payment ledger (A-009) and a new incentive for a malicious provider (ADV-001). A provider could inflate the frozen baseline with self-routed or sponsored traffic, or exploit alias or machine identity handling, to extract top-ups. The canonical model has no TB-008 or threat entry for floor payments, baseline integrity, double-payment across aliases, or admin-endpoint misuse. The changelog also says existing accounting archives do not cover the new financial tables. Fix: add a threat entry and mitigations for baseline manipulation, canonical-machine deduplication, the cumulative pool cap and admin authorization. Confirm that sponsored or self-consumed traffic is handled, and keep payments disabled until that review is done. The code was not supplied, so this finding rests on the changelog description only.
findings.title: New Autopilot daily earnings-floor payout path has no threat-model coverage
